title: Net Exchange piece 8, second call: the table of panels, row by row from the code
purpose: Finish section 2.2 of docs/spec.md, the table of panels of the Net Exchange bureau application, so that every row says exactly which key does what, as the code has it. A first call wrote the table; its review found 29 of 87 rows with a vague Keys cell and at least three rows that contradict the code. facts: HOW A KEY GETS ITS NUMBER, as app/src/web/keys.ts and app/src/web/panel.tsx have it. A panel hands a list of its numbered things to usePicks (which calls numberPicks). Entries that are false, null or undefined are dropped first and hold NO place. Then, in the order of the list: an entry with an explicit 'key' has that key (key 0 is the tenth); every other entry, and every KEPT, takes the next free number counting from 1 and skipping the numbers that explicit keys took; KEPT takes a number and shows nothing, so the things after it keep their numbers; an eleventh thing has no key. The cap shows Ctrl with the number; in the table write the number only, and write the tenth as 0. usePicks returns the number of each id; the JSX shows it with <PickKey n={picks.ID} /> beside the words of the thing.

OTHER WAYS A NUMBER IS GIVEN. <Choices choices={...}> and useChoiceKeys number the choices 1, 2, 3 in the order of the array (panel.tsx). <ChoiceButton number={N}> shows the number it is given. The page buttons of a list come from pagePicks in app/src/web/pages/FindPanels.tsx and the <Pages> element, whose 'before' and 'after' are the words on the two buttons; read them at each use. The lists of Set up share ListPanel in app/src/web/pages/SetUpList.tsx. On Home the Tutorial button and Sign Out carry 9 and 0 from app/src/web/App.tsx.

ENTER AND ESC. On a <Panel>, onSubmit is what Enter does and onBack is where Esc leads; some panels use useBack(FALLBACK), which goes back to the screen the cashier came from and to FALLBACK when the panel was opened by its address. A panel with no onBack has no way back.

requirements.requirement: EVERY ROW REBUILT FROM ITS PANEL'S CODE. Replace the data rows of the table under '### 2.2 The panels'; the header '| Panel | Address | For | What it asks or shows | Keys |' and the rule under it stay. WHAT A ROW IS: a panel is a state of the screen with its own title or question. Every <Panel element in app/src/web outside tutorial belongs to a row; elements that draw the same title for the same purpose (a loading or an error state of one panel) share a row; an element whose title depends on a state gets one row for each state; one element drawn at several addresses gets a row for each address. The sign-in (app/src/web/pages/Login.tsx) and the receipt (app/src/web/pages/Receipt.tsx) are drawn without <Panel and have a row each. A form with two pages of boxes is one row whose Keys cell gives the first page, then '; second page:' and the second. THE CELLS. Panel: the title or question as the cashier reads it, copied from the code, in double quotes, a variable part in capitals ("What do you want to do with CODE?"), followed in parentheses by the name the stage row gives the panel when that differs or when two rows would otherwise have the same Panel cell; no two rows have the same Panel cell. Address: in backticks, the route path as app/src/web/App.tsx writes it, with ':panel', ':statement', ':name' and ':group' written out as their values and ':id' and ':code' left as written; then, inside the backticks, the query that selects this panel when it has one, a variable value in capitals; when the panel is a state of that address with no address of its own, the word (view) after the closing backtick; the sign-in has (signed out) and no backticks. For: 'everyone', 'administrator', 'cashier', or the condition in a few words, read from the guards of the routes, from SET_UP and setUpFor in flows.ts and from the panel's own code. What it asks or shows: one or two sentences in the screen's own words on what is read and what is decided there; name the note 'How this is calculated' where the panel has one. Keys: every numbered thing in the order of its number, each as the number, a space and the words the screen shows beside its cap ('1 Next customer, 2 Print receipt, 3 See the deal'); a box by its label; a thing that is there only in some state with that state in parentheses after its words ('3 Revert (administrator, a deal not reverted)'); a place held for a thing that is away as '(4 held for Make primary)'; a run of list rows as '2-7 the six rows of the page' with what a row opens in parentheses; what differs by role said in the cell ('a cashier has 1 only'). Then 'Enter' and what it does in the words of its button, and 'Esc' and where it leads; 'Esc: no way back' where the panel has none. A panel with nothing to press by number has the two words 'no key' in place of the list of keys. THE FORM OF THE CELL, which a script reads: the keys as entries joined by a comma and a space, each entry beginning with its number (a held place is an entry in parentheses, '(4 held for Make primary)'); a form of two pages has '; second page: ' between the entries of its pages; then '; Enter ' and what it does; then '; Esc ' and where it leads, as the last two parts of the cell. A run of rows is written with a plain hyphen, '2-7', never with another dash. No semicolon stands anywhere else in the cell, and no entry's words begin with a digit. Nothing in the cell is taken from another row or from the first call's table without reading this panel's own code.

requirements.requirement: THE EVIDENCE OF EVERY KEY. results.rows has one entry for every data row of table 2.2, in the order of the table, with: 'panel', the exact text of the row's Panel cell; 'address', the exact text of its Address cell; 'keys_cell', the exact text of its Keys cell; and 'keys', an array with one entry for every key the Keys cell names, in the order of the cell. An entry of 'keys' has: 'key', one of '1' to '9', '0', a run written exactly as in the cell ('2-7'), 'Enter' or 'Esc'; a cell with 'no key' has only its Enter and Esc entries; 'words', the words the cell gives that key; 'held', true for a place that is held and false otherwise; 'file', the path from the repository root; 'line', the number of the line that gives the thing its place or its key: for a numbered thing the line of its entry in the list handed to usePicks or numberPicks, or of its choice in the array handed to <Choices> or useChoiceKeys, or of its <ChoiceButton number=...>, or for a page button the line of the <Pages element or the pagePicks call; for Enter the line where onSubmit (or the panel's own Enter handler) is set; for Esc the line where onBack, useBack or an Escape handler is set, or the line of the <Panel element when there is no way back; and 'code', the text of that line of that file with the white space at its two ends removed, put in by a script that reads the file. Where a number follows from a place in a list, 'place' says which place it is in the list after the dropped entries are left out. Build results.rows with a script and check with it that every 'code' equals its line.
